scenes.say: Ever wondered how containers really differ from virtual machines? Let's break it down.
A virtual machine runs its own operating system and kernel on a hypervisor. A container just shares the host's kernel and runs on a container runtime.

scenes.label: Startup
scenes.sub: VMs boot in minutes; containers in seconds.
scenes.say: VMs can take minutes to start. Containers are ready in seconds.

scenes.label: Size
scenes.sub: VMs use gigabytes; containers use megabytes.
scenes.say: VMs are heavy and use gigabytes of resources. Containers are much lighter, often just megabytes.

scenes.question: Do containers have their own kernel?
scenes.wrong: Yes, each has its own kernel.
scenes.right: No, containers share the host kernel and isolate with namespaces and cgroups.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: Do containers have their own kernel? Remember, they share the host kernel and use namespaces and cgroups for isolation.
